records.title: Flaky test: AutoFlowRunnerTest.incompleteDuration_thenMatch_runsOnceAndPostsOnReady times out intermittently
acceptance_excerpt: No unsynchronized shared counters or fixed-sleep readiness waits in `AutoFlowRunnerTest`
50 consecutive local or CI reruns of `AutoFlowRunnerTest` pass (log attached to the fixing commit or this issue)
`:ai:jvmTest` green in CI
implementation_evidence: Merged PR #124 plus linked local evidence; see handoff validation table
required_validation_notes: `AutoFlowRunnerTest.incompleteDuration_thenMatch_runsOnceAndPostsOnReady` (`ai/src/jvmTest/kotlin/dev/velum/ai/pipeline/AutoFlowRunnerTest.kt`) is flaky. In a dev cloud-agent run it timed out once in `:ai:jvmTest` and passed on rerun (reported by Velum Dev, 2026-10-28). I have not reproduced it myself yet.
Flaky tests make the Android 1.0 ship rule (green CI) unreliable and hide real AutoFlow regressions.
## Likely causes (from reading the test, not yet confirmed)
1. `processCalls` is a plain `var` incremented on the scheduler's thread and polled from the `runBlocking` test thread. There is no `AtomicInteger` or `@Volatile`, so visibility is not guaranteed.

2. The test relies on fixed sleeps (`delay(200)` after `runner.start()`, `delay(400)` for the negative check) to wait for the runner's repository subscription. These waits can be too short under CI load.

3. `runner.actions` is a `MutableSharedFlow` with `replay = 0`. The `async { actions.first { ... } }` subscriber only starts when the test coroutine first suspends, so an emit that happens before then is lost.
4. The scheduler lambda calls nested `runBlocking` on `Dispatchers.Default` threads, and the test's `CoroutineScope` is never cancelled. This can starve the dispatcher when tests run in parallel.
The test passes deterministically: 50 consecutive runs of `./gradlew :ai:jvmTest --tests '*AutoFlowRunnerTest*' --rerun-tasks` with zero failures.
